variables.reason: The problem defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment (arithmetic mean roughness). The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness uses symbols Ra / R_a, gives the same definition (mean absolute deviation of surface height) and lists si_dimension: L with dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0], i.e. a single length dimension and all other base exponents zero. That KB entry therefore directly applies to the Ra in the problem and supports the proposed SI exponents (L=1, others=0).

The problem defines kt as peak-to-valley height (a roughness amplitude length). The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height explicitly lists symbols including kt and defines it as a height difference with si_dimension: L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. That matches the candidate exponents (L=1, others=0) and so pq_peak_to_valley_height applies to kt in the original problem.

The problem defines k_rms as the root-mean-square height, a fluctuation-of-height measure with units of length. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height names k_rms, gives the same definition (RMS fluctuation of surface height) and reports si_dimension: L with dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. This directly supports the proposed SI exponents (L=1, others=0).

Sk is defined in the problem as the third central moment divided by k_rms^3 (surface-height skewness), a standardized (dimensionless) moment. The KB record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness, labels it Sk, and has si_dimension: 1 with dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]. This confirms Sk is dimensionless and matches the candidate exponents (all zeros).

Ku is the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of height fluctuations and therefore dimensionless. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines Ku as surface-height kurtosis with si_dimension: 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], directly supporting the candidate all-zero SI exponents.

ES is given as the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute surface slope) which is a derivative of length with respect to length and hence dimensionless. The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines ES with si_dimension: 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], confirming the candidate zero exponents for all base dimensions.

Po is surface porosity (void fraction), a dimensionless fraction. The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity/void fraction with si_dimension: 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], matching the candidate all-zero SI exponents and applying directly to the Po in the problem.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness ks/Ra is dimensionless as it is a ratio of two lengths (ks and Ra). The input parameters include length measures (Ra, kt, k_rms), dimensionless shape descriptors (Sk, Ku), slope (ES), and porosity (Po). The length parameters have dimension of length, while Sk, Ku, ES, and Po are dimensionless. Therefore, the dimensionless relationship governing ks/Ra can be derived from these inputs.

Ku is the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of height fluctuations and therefore dimensionless. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines Ku as surface-height kurtosis with si_dimension: 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], directly supporting the candidate all-zero SI exponents.

ES is given as the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute surface slope) which is a derivative of length with respect to length and hence dimensionless. The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines ES with si_dimension: 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], confirming the candidate zero exponents for all base dimensions.

Po is surface porosity (void fraction), a dimensionless fraction. The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity/void fraction with si_dimension: 1 and dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,0,0,0], matching the candidate all-zero SI exponents and applying directly to the Po in the problem.
